narrative: The model estimates your probability of failing at 19%. That is a relatively low risk—you are much more likely to pass than fail—but the school is treating it as enough to require remedial courses as a precaution. The strongest factor increasing your risk was that you do not want to continue into higher education; among students who passed, all of them said they did. That contrast was the most important reason the model leaned toward failure. The second most influential factor was your reason for choosing this school: choosing it for its reputation was common among passing students and worked in your favor. The third was your past class failures: you have none, matching the passing average, which also worked in your favor. To improve, focus first on motivation and goals—speak with a counselor about how school connects to higher education, training, or career plans. Also address attendance: 12 absences is well above the passing average of about 4, so attending consistently matters. Keep using your family support and internet access, and maintain a steady study routine.
